doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Agent, pay and the film 'Rules Don't Apply'
summary: No lyricists' union; her UK agent negotiates deals, including a Warren Beatty film song.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Gee. How do you charge for your work? If you are writing lyrics for a cartoon or some Disney thing, there’s the musician’s union, is there a lyricist’s union?
No, sadly there is not. I have an agent in the U.K., Maggie Rockford and if something like that comes along then she negotiates it. And he and I wrote something for the Warren

Beatty movie “Rules Don’t Apply” which is named after a song after we wrote it. It was unfortunately a terrible flop. But it was exciting to do and at the time we made a deal to write it and also I had recorded the song and they had an option to use my version but they decided just to leave Lily Collins’ version as the closing title. So yeah, it’s just a thing that somebody negotiates for you if you have someone to do that, which I do.
